maya_ng: opened PR to update oboro-6b card + catalog: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/4831
maya_ng: Short: clarify seq limits, add tiny throughput row with HW (GPU, batch, seq), switch snippets to Async v4 streaming, call out CPU-quant fallback behavior. Quick review pls.
oliver_su: Skim: card lists "seq_limit: 8192" but bench CSV is for 4096. We shouldn't imply we've validated sustained 8k.
sophie_docs: Suggest wording under Limits: "runtime technical max: 8192 (not validated for sustained high-throughput); recommended prod ceiling: 4096 for latency-sensitive workloads." Also add: "KV cache grows O(seq_len) — enable prefix-caching for repeated contexts."
maya_ng: Current snippet (blocking): ```python
from redwood import Client
client = Client()
resp = client.generate(model="oboro-6b", prompt="Summarize...", max_tokens=128)
print(resp.text)
```
maya_ng: Replacing with Async v4 streaming & param rename: ```python
from redwood import AsyncClient
client = AsyncClient()
async with client.stream_generate(model="oboro-6b", prompt="Summarize...", max_new_tokens=128) as s:
    async for chunk in s:
        print(chunk.text, end="")
```
sophie_docs: Add one-liner about quant fallback: "When CPU fallback is used for quantized variants, expect slower cold-starts and ~3x lower steady throughput."
